log: Working out who would actually buy this
Discovering candidates and exact source URLs (stage 1 of 2)
Fetching up to 10 exact URLs; validating against at most 48,000 characters
Evaluating candidates against 8 fetched pages (stage 2 of 2)

Coverage gaps and failures. (1) No buyer-voice source found for the consultant or agency segment beyond the single quote already in the brief — targeted Reddit and forum searches returned product-comparison and directory pages instead of community discussion, so the client-support-overhead mechanism is still vendor-stated and inferred. (2) No first-person account from any engineering or product lead at a developer-facing company explaining why they removed Google Analytics; the named customers (Ghost, Basecamp, Hugging Face) remain quotes without motive, and the closest substitute is a different company citing hypocrisy in selling privacy software while running GA. (3) No named platform or host publicly describing a white-label integration; that segment rests on vendor documentation only. (4) Enterprise pricing is unpublished, which blocks both the channel and SSO-needing segments from self-qualifying and is a real gating risk, not a copy problem. (5) Nothing found on HIPAA, a BAA, or US data residency for this product, so the healthcare candidate may be structurally incompatible rather than merely unproven. (6) An eighth situation surfaced that I did not promote to a candidate for lack of a credible buyer voice: EU-facing ecommerce merchants reporting 30–50% analytics data loss after installing a consent banner. The supporting figures came from CMP and agency marketing blogs rather than merchants, with only a Shopify Community thread as a first-person signal; worth an explore pass rather than inclusion here. (7) No population counts are available for any segment; all are returned as unknown. (8) Searches were run in English only, which likely under-samples German, French and Dutch municipal and SME discussion where the sovereignty trigger is strongest.
7 audience(s) mapped; 0 worth exploring first. Commercial priority is a hypothesis, not a response-rate forecast.
